ddl:
CREATE TABLE Document (
    Creation_Date DATETIME,
    Document_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Title VARCHAR(255),
    Version_Number VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Author (
    Author_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Date_of_Birth DATETIME,
    Gender VARCHAR(255),
    Name VARCHAR(255),
    Phone_Number VARCHAR(255),
    Position VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Modification_Record (
    Document_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Modification_Content VARCHAR(255),
    Modification_Date DATETIME,
    Modifying_Author_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Version_Number VARCHAR(255),
    PRIMARY KEY (Document_ID, Modification_Date, Modifying_Author_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Document_ID) REFERENCES Document(Document_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Modifying_Author_ID) REFERENCES Author(Author_ID)
);
gold_question: The Technical Document Management Department manages multiple technical documents, and each document is written by multiple authors. A document has a Document ID, Title, Creation Date, and Version Number. An author has an ID, Name, Date of Birth, Gender, Phone Number, and Position. The document version record needs to record the Modification ID, Document ID, Version Number, Modification Date, Modifying Author, and Modification Content.
nl_text: The database name is rschema_0062, and it contains three tables: Document, Author, and Modification_Record. The Document table has four columns: Creation_Date, Document_ID (primary key), Title, and Version_Number. The Author table has six columns: Author_ID (primary key), Date_of_Birth, Gender, Name, Phone_Number, and Position. The Modification_Record table has five columns: Document_ID (foreign key referencing Document.Document_ID), Modification_Content, Modification_Date, Modifying_Author_ID (foreign key referencing Author.Author_ID), and Version_Number. The primary key of the Modification_Record table is a composite key consisting of Document_ID, Modification_Date, and Modifying_Author_ID. The foreign keys in the Modification_Record table reference the Document and Author tables, and the update and delete rules are CASCADE and RESTRICT, respectively.
